issues.problem: The documented enterprise API is hosted at api.coursera.com, not api.coursera.org, and uses the /ent/api prefix.
The request uses the wrong host and omits the required /ent prefix. Its sample program object also includes slug, which is not part of the current documented BusinessProgram schema.
issues.suggestion: Use curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN" "https://api.coursera.com/ent/api/businesses.v1/YOUR_ORG_ID/programs" and model program fields on the documented id, name, tagline, and url schema.

issues.problem: GoldRush ended its permanent free tier in 2025. Current general access starts with a 14-day trial containing 25,000 credits, so describing a continuing Premium free tier is outdated.
issues.suggestion: Set free_tier to false and describe the 14-day, 25,000-credit free trial. Current self-serve paid tiers include Vibe Coding at $10/month and Professional at $250/month.

issues.problem: Current plan throughput is publicly documented, contrary to the entry.
issues.suggestion: State 4 RPS for the free trial and Vibe Coding plan, 50 RPS for Professional, and custom limits for Inner Circle.

issues.problem: Authenticated Cargo registry operations send the API token directly as the Authorization header value, not as a Bearer token.
issues.suggestion: Say that write operations use Authorization: YOUR_CRATES_IO_TOKEN, normally handled by Cargo credential providers.

issues.problem: The crates.io data-access policy publishes a maximum API rate of one request per second.
issues.suggestion: Set this to 1 request/second and mention that bulk users should prefer database dumps or the registry index where appropriate.

issues.problem: crates.io requires API clients to supply a descriptive User-Agent identifying the application and providing contact information; the bare curl example does not comply with that policy and may be rejected.
Crawlbase currently publishes a Crawling API limit of 20 requests per second per token, so 'not published' is incorrect.
issues.suggestion: Set this to 20 requests/second per token, noting that plan concurrency and certain specialized endpoints may have separate limits.

issues.problem: Without format=json, the endpoint returns the target response body directly and places metadata in headers. The shown JSON wrapper is therefore inconsistent with the request, and pc_status is an obsolete field name; current responses use cb_status.
issues.suggestion: Add &format=json to the request and show a response containing original_status, cb_status, url, and body.

issues.problem: The free-tier limit is currently published rather than unknown.
issues.suggestion: Set it to 100 API hits per day on the Lifetime Free plan.

issues.problem: Crossref now publishes explicit REST API limits, so the claim that no authoritative limits are published is outdated.
issues.suggestion: State that single-record requests are limited to 5 RPS in the public pool and 10 RPS in the polite pool; list requests are limited to 1 RPS public and 3 RPS polite. Also observe the concurrency and rate-limit response headers.

issues.problem: CryptoCompare/CCData is now branded as CoinDesk Data. The entry presents the former brand as though it were still the current product name.
issues.suggestion: Rename it to CoinDesk Data (formerly CryptoCompare/CCData), while identifying min-api.cryptocompare.com as the legacy Min API interface.

issues.problem: The vague ongoing free-tier claim is outdated. CoinDesk Data announced retirement of its free API tier effective May 21, 2026; current Personal access is subscription-based and described using capped lifetime calls rather than a recurring free quota.
issues.suggestion: Remove the recurring free-tier claim and record the exact current Personal subscription and lifetime-call allowance shown during signup, with Start-Up and Enterprise pricing listed as contact-based.

issues.problem: A free self-serve API key by itself no longer guarantees data access; accounts without an applicable API subscription stopped receiving data after May 21, 2026.
issues.suggestion: Retain API-key authentication but state that an active CoinDesk Data API subscription or entitled Personal plan is required.

issues.problem: The paid-plan names and prices are stale and internally contradictory. Current published monthly plans are Small $9.99, Medium $39.99, and Large $79.99, not Basic $10, Pro $30, and Business $99.99 or a starting price of $11.99.
issues.suggestion: Use the current Small, Medium, and Large plan names and their displayed billing-cycle prices, noting that annual billing can differ.

issues.problem: A per-minute limit is publicly specified for the free plan.
issues.suggestion: State 300 requests/month and 10 requests/minute for Free; current paid plans advertise no per-minute rate limit while retaining monthly quotas.

issues.problem: The current free Developer plan provides 1,000 requests per day, not 600.
issues.suggestion: Set the free-tier limit to 1,000 requests/day.

issues.problem: The stated 600-request daily limit is outdated.
issues.suggestion: Set the free-plan quota to 1,000 requests/day; paid plans use their published monthly quotas.
